title: Reconcile attempts on daemon restart instead of purging every worker
description:
Objective: stop a daemon restart from yanking a task away from a CLI that is still running. packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:501 calls purgeAllWorkers on every start, and state/workerStore.ts:305 deletes every worker record and releases their tasks without first establishing that the external processes exited. A restart during a long build therefore hands live work to someone else.

Deliverable: on startup, attempts in phase running are moved to reconciling rather than being destroyed, and their tasks are held from reassignment while reconciling. A runner reattaches by presenting its attempt id plus process start time and host; a successful reattach returns the attempt to running. An attempt confirmed dead, or one that stays unreattached past a configurable reconcile window, is closed and gets exactly one successor generation.

Not in scope: heartbeat semantics, which are the sibling task. Preserve stable worker identity across the restart by persisting it separately from the attempt, and preserve the existing rule that a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker: the reconcile window must not become an idle-based auto-release for WORKING or PLANNING.

Unskips the acceptance case "restarting only the daemon during a long build preserves ownership".

Verification: npx vitest run src/state/workerStore.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from packages/moe-daemon.
definitionOfDone: Daemon startup moves running attempts to reconciling and holds their tasks from reassignment instead of releasing them
A runner that reattaches with a matching attempt id, process start time and host returns the attempt to running and keeps the task assigned
An attempt confirmed dead, or unreattached past the configurable reconcile window, is closed and permits exactly one successor generation
Stable worker identity survives the restart and is persisted separately from the attempt record
The reconcile window is a settings key with a documented default and is never applied to a live reattached attempt, so no idle-based auto-release is introduced for WORKING or PLANNING
The acceptance case for restart during a long build is unskipped and passes unchanged
npx vitest run src/state/workerStore.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts passes and npm test in packages/moe-daemon stays green
taskRails: Do not reintroduce idle-based auto-release for WORKING or PLANNING; a quiet build is not evidence of a dead worker.
REVIEW's existing reviewStaleTimeoutMs self-heal stays exactly as it is.
Reassignment must establish the old process stopped, or contain its writes; a JSON record alone does not stop a running CLI.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE HELD-OUT CASE AS THE CONTRACT (read-only, no edits). This card owns unskipping the fourth acceptance case and its assertions may not be edited, so it is the specification and it overrides any wording here. Read src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts from the describe at line 1607 to line 1835, plus the helpers it uses: `startDaemonChild`, `killDaemonAbruptly`, `daemonTool`, `toolResult`, `toolRefusal`, `spawnOwned`, `isPidAlive`, `readBytes` and `listRecords`. Note that it drives the REAL startup path, a daemon child spawned through the installed CLI, never a StateManager reload, and that it has a 240 second timeout because it spawns a genuine long-running process. Extract the exact contract: a new tool `moe.reattach_attempt` taking taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt and host; a successful reattach leaves phase `running`, the task WORKING and assigned, and the worker record's currentTaskId intact; a reattach whose processStartedAt OR host differs is refused with numeric code -32002 and codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH`; a competing claim during the hold is refused with -32002 and codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_RECONCILING`, with the attempt id inside the message; and every refusal is byte-pure, asserted on the task file, the worker file and the attempt file. Note two details that will otherwise be missed: `toolRefusal` also asserts a `tool` field naming the refusing tool, so check how it reads that off the error payload and make sure both refusals carry it; and the first daemon calls reattach on an attempt that is ALREADY running, which must succeed and leave it running, so reattach is idempotent for the running phase. Finally note what the fixture proves about liveness: the worker has been quiet for three hours and the build emits nothing, yet ownership must hold, so nothing in this work may consult lastActivityAt. Then read the code you will change: `purgeAllWorkers` at src/state/workerStore.ts line 305, its call site at src/index.ts line 501, the attempt store's phase setter, and the claim path's existing finalizing refusal, which is the pattern the reconciling refusal should follow. Read the task comment on this card recording the scope split before you plan any window or sweep behaviour: those two definition-of-done items now belong to task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c and must NOT be built here. Produce no diff in this step.

CAPTURE THE RED PROOF BEFORE CHANGING ANYTHING. Unskip only the fourth acceptance case by changing its `it.skip` to `it`, touching not one assertion, and run `npx vitest run src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts` from packages/moe-daemon. SAVE the failing output: it is the epic rail's fails-on-old-behaviour evidence and the definition-of-done item that the case passes unedited. The expected first failure is the counterexample the case names, a purged owner: the second daemon's startup deletes the worker and releases the task while the build is still alive. Record which assertion fails first. Be aware this case spawns real processes and takes minutes; if the harness cannot spawn a daemon child in this environment, say so explicitly in the step note rather than editing the case or marking it skipped again. Then create src/state/workerStore.test.ts, which this card's verification command names and which does not exist yet, using the existing ToolTestHarness convention. It covers what the slow end-to-end case cannot isolate, all against the store rather than a spawned daemon: a worker owning a running attempt survives startup reconciliation with its record and currentTaskId intact and its task still WORKING and assigned; that attempt's phase becomes exactly `reconciling`; a worker owning NO attempt is still purged and its task still released exactly as today, which is the legacy path that must not regress; a worker whose attempt is already closed is likewise purged; a task held in reconciling is refused to a competing claimer with the exact code name; and a worker quiet for hours is held regardless, which is the test that fails if anyone reintroduces a liveness inference. Assert exact phase strings and exact code names, never truthiness.

RECONCILE ON STARTUP INSTEAD OF DESTROYING. Add one exported helper to packages/moe-daemon/src/state/attemptStore.ts that moves every attempt currently in the running phase to reconciling, reusing the existing phase setter so the store keeps its single write-then-publish ordering, and returning what it moved so the caller can decide which workers to spare. Give it a comment stating plainly what the phase means: the daemon has lost sight of this execution and is holding the task until a runner proves the process is still there, which is not the same as believing it is alive. Then change `purgeAllWorkers` in src/state/workerStore.ts. It currently deletes every worker file, clears the map and releases every orphaned assignment. It must now spare a worker that owns a non-closed attempt: keep its record on disk and in the map, keep its currentTaskId, and leave its task WORKING and assigned rather than routing it through the release path. The worker record is what the definition of done means by stable identity persisted separately from the attempt, so it is deliberately not derived from the attempt file. Every worker with no attempt, or only closed ones, keeps today's purge and release behaviour exactly, because that is the legacy path for every project that predates attempts. Keep the existing per-worker error handling: one unwritable record must not abort startup for the rest of the fleet. In src/index.ts, at the startup call site around line 501, run the reconcile pass before the purge so the purge can see which attempts were held, and confirm while you are there that the state load which populates the attempts map already runs before both. Nothing here may consult lastActivityAt or any other idle signal.

REFUSE A COMPETING CLAIM WHILE AN ATTEMPT IS RECONCILING. In src/tools/claimNextTask.ts add a refusal that mirrors the finalizing one already in that file: same position, inside the exclusive section and before any ranking, eligibility scan or assignment write, so a refused claim can never have changed an owner. It differs in scope, and the difference matters: the finalizing hold is scoped to the calling worker, while this one is scoped to the TASK, because the whole point is to stop a DIFFERENT worker taking a task whose owner is still out there. Throw a MoeError with the STATE_CONFLICT code, codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_RECONCILING`, a message naming the attempt id, and a context carrying the attempt id, its generation, the task and the holding worker. Follow whatever the finalizing refusal does to surface the `tool` field that the acceptance helper asserts, so both refusals look the same on the wire. Do not let this refusal fire for the attempt's own owner reattaching through the claim path: reattachment has its own tool and this refusal is for third parties. Change nothing about claimable statuses, dependency gating, ranking, the alreadyAssigned resume or the attempt opening that already exists in this file. This is the error handling path the acceptance case exercises with worker-X, and it asserts the files are byte-identical afterwards, so the refusal must happen before any write.

WRITE THE REATTACH TOOL. Create packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/reattachAttempt.ts following the shape of the neighbouring tool modules: an exported factory returning a ToolDefinition named `moe.reattach_attempt`, an input schema declaring taskId, workerId, runnerId, attemptId, generation, processStartedAt and host with additionalProperties false, and a handler whose whole body runs inside state.runExclusive. Do NOT mark it blocking: it never parks. Handler order: validate the inputs and refuse malformed ones as invalid input; load the attempt by id and refuse a missing one or one whose taskId does not match, by name; then compare the presented identity against the stored record. The identity is the attempt id, the generation, the recorded processStartedAt and the recorded host, and ALL of them must match: the acceptance case refuses a start time off by sixty seconds and refuses a different host with the same start time, both with codeName exactly `ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH` and the STATE_CONFLICT code. Compare the timestamps as exact recorded strings rather than by parsing to a date, so a re-serialised value cannot widen the match. On a mismatch throw before any write, because the case asserts byte-identical files afterwards. On a match, move the attempt to running through the store's phase setter and return the attempt id, generation and phase; an attempt already running is a no-op that returns the same success, which is what the first daemon in the case relies on. Leave the task and the worker record alone: the point of the hold is that they were never disturbed, and writing them here would be a second source of truth. Say in a comment what this tool does and does not prove: a matching process start time and host narrow which process the runner is talking about, they do not establish that it is alive, and nothing may treat them as proof. Then register the tool in getTools() in src/tools/index.ts, because an unregistered tool is silently invisible to MCP.

DOCUMENT THE TOOL AND THE RESTART CONTRACT. Add a section for `moe.reattach_attempt` to docs/MCP_SERVER.md alongside the other lifecycle tools, in the existing section format: purpose, parameters, returns, notes. The notes must carry what a runner cannot guess: that a daemon restart parks every running attempt in the reconciling phase and holds its task rather than releasing it, which is a deliberate change from the old purge-everything startup; that the runner reattaches by presenting the attempt id, generation, recorded process start time and host, and that all of them must match exactly; that a mismatch and a competing claim are both refused by name, with the two code names spelled out; that reattaching an already-running attempt is a safe no-op, so a retry after a lost response is fine; and the honest boundary that a matching start time and host narrow which process is meant but prove nothing about whether it is alive. Add one line to the daemon-lifecycle prose noting that the startup purge now spares a worker that owns a non-closed attempt, so worker identity survives a restart. Do not document the reconcile window or any timeout here: that belongs to the sibling card task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c. Documentation only, no behaviour change.

RUN THE NAMED GATE AND THE FULL SUITE WITH RECORDED EVIDENCE. From packages/moe-daemon run this card's own command first: `npx vitest run src/state/workerStore.test.ts src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts`. The fourth acceptance case must pass with its assertions untouched; if it does not, fix the production code, never the case. Allow for its 240 second budget and real process spawning, and if the environment genuinely cannot spawn daemon children, report that in the completion rather than claiming a pass. Then run the whole package suite from the repo root, `npm --prefix packages/moe-daemon test` on Unix and the same with npm.cmd on Windows, plus `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`. Capture each exit code separately from any filtered output, because a grep pipeline swallows it on this box, and require exit 0 everywhere with counts strictly greater than the baseline. Watch the restart-sensitive suites specifically: anything covering purgeAllWorkers, claim behaviour and daemon startup, because sparing a worker changes a path that every other test boots through. Confirm the acceptance file's other cases keep their existing skip state and still collect. Keep the exact commands, exit codes and counts for the verification argument of moe.complete_task, and keep the step-2 red output as the fails-on-old-behaviour proof.

ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW, THEN HAND OFF. Read the diff as an attacker and confirm each of these or fix it: a worker owning a non-closed attempt genuinely survives startup with its file, its map entry and its currentTaskId, and its task is neither released nor re-routed; a worker with no attempt is still purged exactly as before, so no legacy project regresses; nothing anywhere consults lastActivityAt or any idle signal to decide the hold, which the three-hour-quiet fixture is there to catch; the reconciling claim refusal is scoped by task rather than by worker, or a third party walks straight in; both refusals throw before any write and leave every file byte-identical; the identity comparison requires the attempt id, the generation, the process start time AND the host, with the timestamp compared as the exact stored string; reattaching an already-running attempt is a no-op rather than an error; the tool is registered and not marked blocking; and the reconcile window, the successor generation and any sweep were left entirely to the sibling card. Confirm the file count is the nine in scope. Then call moe.complete_task with the verification evidence from the previous step, list every modified path in modifiedFiles, and tell QA two things plainly: that two definition-of-done items were moved to task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c under the operator-approved split recorded in this card's comment and are deliberately absent here, and that the restart hold narrows which process a runner means but never establishes that it is alive, so a genuinely dead runner still parks its task until that sibling card lands.

SCOPE SPLIT, operator-approved 2026-09-11. This card needed 10 distinct files, the size gate's hard ceiling, so the give-up half moved to a new sibling: task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c, "Close an attempt that never reattaches and allow one successor", which dependsOn this card.

Two definition-of-done items moved there verbatim and are NOT deliverable here. QA should not fail this card for them:
- "An attempt confirmed dead, or unreattached past the configurable reconcile window, is closed and permits exactly one successor generation"
- "The reconcile window is a settings key with a documented default and is never applied to a live reattached attempt, so no idle-based auto-release is introduced for WORKING or PLANNING"

This card keeps the restart hold, the reattach surface and the claim refusal, which is exactly what its acceptance case (src/delivery/acceptance.test.ts, describe at line 1607) drives end to end. That case never waits for a reconcile window and never infers death from lastActivityAt, so it is fully satisfiable without the moved items.

Remaining definition-of-done here: startup moves running attempts to reconciling and holds their tasks; a matching reattach returns the attempt to running with the task still assigned; stable worker identity survives the restart, persisted separately from the attempt; the acceptance case is unskipped and passes unchanged; and the named verification command plus the full package suite stay green.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Planning all seven definition-of-done items in one card: it needed 10 distinct files, the size gate's hard ceiling, with a real-process acceptance case that takes minutes. The operator was asked and chose to split, so the give-up half is now task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c and this card keeps exactly what its acceptance case drives. (2) Deriving worker identity from the attempt record rather than sparing the worker file: rejected, because the definition of done asks for identity persisted SEPARATELY from the attempt, and the acceptance case asserts the worker file's currentTaskId directly after the restart. (3) Scoping the reconciling claim refusal to the calling worker, mirroring the finalizing hold: rejected outright, and worth stating because it is the obvious copy-paste error — the finalizing hold stops a worker starting more work, while this one stops a DIFFERENT worker taking a task whose owner is still out there, so it must be scoped by task. (4) Parsing the recorded process start time to a date before comparing: rejected, since a re-serialised value could widen the match; compare the exact stored string. (5) Having reattach also rewrite the task or worker record: rejected, because the whole claim of the hold is that neither was disturbed, and writing them would create a second source of truth. (6) Consulting lastActivityAt to decide whether to hold: forbidden by a task rail and by the fixture, whose worker has been quiet for three hours and must still keep its task.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: The acceptance case at line 1607 is the real specification and is already in the tree. It drives the genuine startup path through a spawned daemon child rather than a StateManager reload, spawns a real silent build process, kills the daemon abruptly, and asserts byte-identical task, worker and attempt files across every refusal. It requires a tool this card's description never names, `moe.reattach_attempt`, with the full identity tuple. Its `toolRefusal` helper asserts a `tool` field on the error alongside code and codeName, so both refusals must carry it the way the existing finalizing refusal does. The first daemon in the case reattaches an attempt that is already running, which pins reattach as idempotent for that phase. On the production side, purgeAllWorkers at workerStore.ts line 305 deletes every worker file, clears the map and releases assignments through nextStatusForRelease, with a deliberate per-worker try/catch so one bad record cannot abort startup; its call site is src/index.ts line 501, and the state load that populates the attempts map runs before it. The attempt store's phase setter already treats a repeated phase as a no-op and closed as terminal, so reconciling and running transitions need no new store primitive beyond one pass helper. src/state/sweeps.ts exists and is where the sibling card's window belongs, not here. src/state/workerStore.test.ts does not exist yet and this card's verification command names it, so it is created here.
planningNotes.risks: The single most likely defect is scoping the reconciling refusal by worker instead of by task, because the finalizing refusal directly above it does exactly that and reads as the pattern to copy. Second is reintroducing a liveness inference: any lastActivityAt check added to the hold passes casual review and fails the three-hour-quiet fixture, and a task rail forbids it. Third is the byte-purity requirement: the case compares raw file bytes after each refusal, so a stray activity row, timestamp or defensive rewrite anywhere in the refusal path breaks it. Sparing a worker from the purge changes a path every other test boots through, so watch the full suite rather than just the named files. The acceptance case spawns real processes with a 240 second budget; if the environment cannot spawn daemon children, that must be reported honestly rather than papered over. Finally, do not overstate the result: matching a process start time and host narrows which process a runner means and proves nothing about liveness, and until the sibling card lands a genuinely dead runner parks its task indefinitely — both belong in the completion summary.

completionSummary:
A daemon restart now HOLDS a live worker's task instead of purging it.

Startup order in src/index.ts is now load -> reconcileRunningAttempts -> purgeAllWorkers. The new attemptStore helper parks every `running` attempt in `reconciling`, and purgeAllWorkers then SPARES any seat owning a non-closed attempt: worker file, map entry and currentTaskId survive, and its task stays WORKING and assigned rather than being released. Every worker with no attempt, or only closed ones, is purged exactly as before (the legacy path). Spared seats also keep their team membership.

New tool moe.reattach_attempt returns a reconciling attempt to `running`. Identity = attempt id + generation + recorded processStartedAt + recorded host, all four required, timestamp compared as the EXACT stored string (a re-serialised same-instant value is refused). Mismatch -> -32002/ATTEMPT_IDENTITY_MISMATCH. Already-running is a byte-identical no-op, so a retry after a lost response is safe. It writes ONLY the attempt: the task and worker record were never disturbed and writing them would be a second source of truth. workerId/runnerId are deliberately NOT compared (claim_next_task stores runnerId = workerId, so comparing would refuse every real reattach) - pinned by a regression test.

claim_next_task refuses a competing claim on a held task with -32002/ATTEMPT_RECONCILING, scoped BY TASK not by caller (the finalizing hold above it is by worker; copying that scope would let a third party walk in), thrown before any ranking/eligibility/write.

TWO THINGS QA SHOULD KNOW, PLAINLY:
1. SCOPE SPLIT (operator-approved 2026-09-11, recorded in this card's comment). Two DoD items moved verbatim to task-d7fa98f4e43d434a96cad9440b153f1c and are DELIBERATELY ABSENT here: the confirmed-dead/unreattached close with one successor generation, and the reconcile-window settings key. Please do not fail this card for them. sweeps.ts has zero changes.
2. HONEST BOUNDARY. A matching process start time and host NARROW WHICH P
